clue.text: German composer repelled English during conflict

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits during, i.e. inside, the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the abbreviation is written backwards

explanation.surface: A German composer shunned the English while the two nations were at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns ENG round to GNE, and 'during' puts that inside WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the nineteenth-century German creator of the Ring cycle operas.

clue.text: Taking in people from the Middle East, we go after the ladies

indicators.note: the word we takes in, i.e. encloses, the Gulf nationals

parts.note: taken as written
Omanis are natives of Oman, on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A man boasts of welcoming Middle Eastern guests while also chasing women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in' puts OMANIS between the W and E of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase women persistently for casual affairs is a verb with exactly this meaning.

clue.text: Boatman going astray in old region

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boatman gets lost in some ancient territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' rearranges the nine letters of OLD and REGION; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian oarsman propelling a canal boat with a single pole-like oar is this.

clue.text: Get this, in revenge

indicators.note: in means the four letters sit inside the single word revenge

explanation.surface: A command to grasp something tucked inside the idea of retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'revenge', and 'get even' is itself a phrase meaning take revenge, so the whole clue both hides and defines the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To get square with someone who wronged you is to settle the score, a phrase meaning retaliation.

clue.text: Doctor observed working amid BSE outbreak

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, meaning observed

indicators.note: amid means the short word for working sits among the scrambled disease letters
an outbreak is a breaking out, suggesting the letters burst into a new order

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A vet or physician watched while working in the middle of a mad-cow epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, the British 'mad cow' disease. 'outbreak' turns BSE into BES, and 'amid' puts ON inside it: B(ON)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a surgeon or physician, from the days of amputation, is this word.

clue.text: Notice youngster making an entrance in panto

indicators.note: the boy is making an entrance into the advertisement word, going inside it

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a lad is a youngster
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotting a boy actor coming on stage in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making an entrance' puts LAD inside AD, giving ALADD, then IN. A panto (pantomime) is the British family stage show staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The tale of the lamp and genie is one of the best-known British Christmas pantomime titles.

clue.text: TV programme runs into a lot of trouble

indicators.note: into means the cricket letter goes inside the phrase for trouble

parts.note: big bother is a lot of trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A television show gets badly into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside BIG BOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reality show in which housemates are filmed constantly, named after Orwell's watchful dictator.

clue.text: Report from northern area of France

parts.note: the Oise is a French department north of Paris

explanation.surface: A bulletin comes in from the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, as of a gun firing, so it is a sound.

clue.text: Very good pie crusts, food for junior

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
a pie's top crusts are its lids

explanation.surface: Excellent pastry tops make good eating for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' joins the pieces in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies are weaned from milk onto mashed and solid foods, so these are infant fare.

clue.text: African sport a boy gets excited about

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the sport's abbreviation
getting excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: A boy gets worked up over a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets excited' turns A BOY into YOBA, and 'about' wraps that around RU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yoruba are a large West African people of Nigeria, and the word also names them or their language.

clue.text: Mass gathering of nations to protect European state

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

indicators.note: to protect means the jumbled letters surround and shield the single letter
a gathering brings things together in a new arrangement, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A large assembly of countries shields a European state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' rearranges NATIONS into INNSOTA, and 'to protect' puts E inside it after INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state whose capital is Saint Paul.

clue.text: Poorly after Greek barbecue

indicators.note: after places the word for poorly following the Greek abbreviation

parts.note: ill means poorly

explanation.surface: A Greek feels unwell after a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat over direct heat outdoors is to broil, a verb shared by both words.

clue.text: Time to clear the centre of Northampton?

indicators.note: clearing the centre means removing everything but the first two and last two letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a Northampton town-centre redevelopment is due.
explanation.walkthrough: Northampton is an English county town. Strip its middle RTHAMPT and NO and ON remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a time of day.

clue.text: He risked going round about on greyish-brown ass

indicators.note: on places the colour word first, with the rest built on after it

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the pronoun
going round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dared means risked
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man gambled by riding round on a grey-brown donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns DARED into DERAD, and 'about' puts it around HE: DER(HE)AD. 'ass' is the definition, not the donkey it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a fool, and a dimwit or blockhead is the same sort of person.

clue.text: Note penned by insurance man for meeting

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the note sits inside the phrase

parts.note: cover is insurance protection
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: An insurance salesman writes a memo for an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like 'written by', but it means enclosed: N goes into COVER GENT after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that come together at a point are coming together, so 'meeting' as an adjective.

clue.text: Short trip to Australia with a philosophical type

parts.note: a spin is a short drive or outing
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker takes a quick jaunt down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker.

clue.text: Recording that's presumably not sound as a bell

parts.note: no means not, a negative
ting is the sound a small bell makes

explanation.surface: A recording session that is not perfectly sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for perfectly healthy, but it means the noise a bell makes; 'presumably' marks the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing something down to remember it is making a note, so recording.

clue.text: Short cut for yours truly

definitions.meaning: a very close crop with the shortest clipper guard on a barber's shears
oneself, me, as one looks after oneself first

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' suggests a quicker route, but it is a haircut, the closest clipper setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The barber's closest clipper setting and slang for oneself share this name.

clue.text: Court case about bribe finishing early

indicators.note: about means the word for case goes around the shortened bribe

parts.note: a trial is a court case

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: bung is British slang for a bribe

explanation.surface: A judge's case concerns a bribe being wound up ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' cuts BUNG (British slang for a bribe) to BUN, and 'about' puts TRIAL around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel set up to adjudicate disputes is a court of a kind.

clue.text: British partygoer with extra bottle?

parts.note: a raver is a lively partygoer

explanation.surface: A British reveller brings along another bottle of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, not a drinks bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle means courage in British slang, so more of it means more courageous.

clue.text: Brazilian port, in our opinion, is disorderly

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
to us means in our opinion, as in it seems to us

explanation.surface: We think the Brazilian city is lawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, wild crowd is unruly in the way the definition describes.

clue.text: Guide round American ship

indicators.note: round means the word for guide goes around the short American

parts.note: steer means guide

explanation.surface: Someone directs an American vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel powered by steam is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Given place to sit, daughter has moved up, calm and unhurried

indicators.note: in a down answer, moving up means shifting the letter earlier in the word

parts.note: seated means given a place to sit

explanation.surface: A girl shown to her seat shifts up, quiet and composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has moved up' moves the D of SEATED two places earlier, giving SE-D-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed and leisurely manner is unhurried and placid.

clue.text: Top journalist looked…

parts.note: a star is a top performer
ed, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A leading reporter gazed on, the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazing fixedly is looking, in the past tense.

clue.text: Golfer is good in match, having right set of clubs

indicators.note: in means the single letter sits inside the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as a cup tie
woods are a set of golf clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer plays well in a tournament, with the right equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good in match' puts G inside TIE, giving TIGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is a famous American golf champion.

clue.text: … set to develop further without wife

indicators.note: without means the letter for wife is taken out

parts.note: to grow up is to develop further

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone is set to mature without a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of people or things is a collection or cluster.

clue.text: Basil, perhaps, is a bit feather-brained

indicators.note: a bit means a small part of the following words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A man called Basil is somewhat scatterbrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' looks like a man's name, but it is the culinary plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a leafy culinary plant used for flavouring.

clue.text: Announced promising player's transfer

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a seed is a promising player ranked in a tournament

explanation.surface: A rising star's move to another club was made public.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over territory or rights is to give it up to another party.

clue.text: River about to swamp house at end of garden

indicators.note: to swamp means to engulf, so the short word goes around the others

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: at end of means the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A river is about to flood a house at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swamp' puts HO and N (the end of 'garden') inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone flows from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Film paid for by municipality?

definitions.meaning: a 1949 musical with Gene Kelly and Frank Sinatra
at the council's expense, the city footing the bill

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means out enjoying nightlife; the question mark marks the literal reading of the local authority paying.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kelly–Sinatra musical title and a phrase for something charged to the council.

clue.text: Terrible dispute involving English substitute

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters take in the single letter
terrible suggests something badly handled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dreadful row involves an English stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges DISPUTE, and 'involving' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as stand-in, so a verb meaning replace temporarily.

clue.text: Happened to live near mountain

indicators.note: near places the word for live next to the hill word

parts.note: be means exist or live
a fell is a hill or mountain in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone got to live close to a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: A FELL is a hill or mountain in the English Lake District and north.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurred or took place is what this past-tense verb means.
